I added `migrations/003_exports_status_default.sql` and left `001_init.sql` alone, because migrations are append-only and 001 has already run in prod. I haven't run the migration.

The migration does three things, in this order:
1. It sets `status` to `'queued'` on existing rows where it's NULL. This has to come first, or the `not null` step would fail on those rows.
2. It sets the column default to `'queued'`.
3. It sets the column to `not null`.

Existing NULL rows will become `'queued'`. If any of them are old exports that actually finished or failed, you may want a different backfill value.

Separately, you may want to check which code path inserts exports with a NULL status. After this change, an insert that explicitly passes NULL will fail instead of silently storing it. Inserts that leave `status` out will get `'queued'`.
